body: - **Means 1, a no-network namespace — BUILDABLE unprivileged, REHEARSABLE under the fake agent on this host.** `unshare --user --map-current-user --net` and `bwrap --unshare-net --dev-bind / /` both run as uid 1000 with no root and no system-wide change (measured: `id -u` 1000 inside; `ip -o link` shows only `lo`; a TCP connect to the API host fails, `curl` exit 7). **What it still lets the CLI reach:** with `unshare` alone, the HOST'S RESOLVER — a name lookup crosses through systemd-resolved's Unix socket (measured: `getent hosts api.anthropic.com` answered inside), so the API host names leave the host as DNS queries; with `bwrap … --tmpfs /run/systemd/resolve` the resolver socket is hidden and the lookup fails (measured: `getent` exit 2), leaving every other filesystem Unix socket the child's paths can name (the session bus and the like under the kept `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, which also holds viola's own socket directory, needed). The child stays in the rig's pid namespace and keeps uid 1000, so viola's socket-directory, peer-euid and pid-plus-start-time checks see what they see today — unmeasured under the wrap, the first thing its rehearsal reads.

- **Means 2, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at a closed port — NOT a containment.** It moves only the Messages API: every other host the CLI calls on start (the OAuth profile, the feature-flag fetch, telemetry, the update check) still leaves the host, and the token goes into a request to a local port any later listener could hold. It also widens the rig's closed kept-name list (`isolate.rs:24-32`) by a host-network value.

- **How a start is KNOWN to have been contained (a predicate that can fail):** the child's `/proc/<pid>/ns/net` link differs from the rig's own (measured: `net:[4026533305]` inside against `net:[4026531833]` outside) → `net-ns: own`, red `shared`; and the turn ends in a StopFailure, never a Stop (a model reply reads red: the API was reached).

- **What the CLI is expected to do on a lost connection (static, 2.1.328):** the request fails at the connect; the CLI retries (10 by default, its reconnect budget 0 offline), then ends the turn with an API-error message whose `error` word is `server_error` (refused, unreachable and unresolvable alike) and fires StopFailure once with that word; a turn must be in flight — StopFailure fires only from a turn's request. The retry delays could not be read reliably from the minified bundle: the turn-end time is a reading the start records, bounded by the rig's `--deadline` (default 600 s).

- **Time per start:** the start and first settle as `CX` (under a minute measured on `L2`), the send, then the retries — estimated one to three minutes, unmeasured — and the teardown: about five minutes, inside the 600 s deadline. No API request reaches Anthropic, so a contained start spends no account usage.

- **Credentials (the directive's item 3):** the contained child neither authenticates nor is refused: it loads the rig's 0600 copy of the OAuth credentials from its private config and sends no request that leaves the host. The rig reads the real `~/.claude/.credentials.json` once (the token window, `isolate::read_credentials`), stamps `~/.claude.json` before and after read-only, writes nothing under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`; the wrap adds no read or write there.

- Does CI's `ubuntu-latest` carry `bwrap` and admit an unprivileged user namespace? → blocks: plan-decision (whether the wrapped rehearsal is a CI case or a local gate entry before the live start, the CI rehearsal then running the arm unwrapped) — asked of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up (inputs#I1).

- Does the CLI's first frame inside the sandbox reach the input box with the used-config markers seeded (no offline modal)? → blocks: implementation-scope — unmeasurable with no start; the live start's first predicate reads it, red `shape` before any send.

   `(architecture · decision/fake-agent-hook-panic-seam)` history: a seam is an argv option, never an env read). Its
   payload is the rehearsal's own synthetic `StopFailure.<variant>.json`, planted in a copy of a recorded set
   (testing.md Test data: a fixtures root for a case that sends after the first turn starts as a copy of the
   recorded set). No recorded set gains a StopFailure file.

4. **The arm and its labels.**
   - `Arm::SF`, word `sf`; labels `SF` and its spare `SF-2` in `of_label`.
   - Its wrapped name `sf-probe`; `trusted`, `marker_seed` and `has_vhome` as `CX`.
   - In the live verb, the wrapped arm's `--model haiku` (`viola-live-rig.rs:239-240`).
   - The doc lines name it (`mod.rs:157-162`, `viola-live-rig.rs:6-11`), with a row in the label test
     (`mod.rs:2321-2330` shape).

5. **The sandbox (test-only host dependency `bwrap`, `inputs#I3` item 4).**
   - A rehearsal option `--contain` (rehearse only). Every live `SF` start is contained, never by an option.
   - Before the ledger line, a contained start resolves `bwrap` on the rig's own `PATH` to an absolute path and
     runs one bounded no-op probe through it. The probe reads `/proc/self/ns/net` inside against the rig's own.
   - `bwrap` absent, a non-zero probe, or the same namespace → `refused: sandbox`, exit 3, uncounted, before any
     ledger line `(inputs#I3 item 4)`.
   - The contained child is spawned as `<bwrap> --unshare-net --die-with-parent --dev-bind / / --tmpfs
     /run/systemd/resolve --tmpfs /tmp --bind <scratch root> <scratch root> -- <viola> --home <vhome> run sf-probe
     -- <claude> --model haiku`: a direct spawn, no shell, every element one argv element.
   - The scratch root is rebound after `/tmp` is privatised, since the rig's scratch base lies under `/tmp`
     (`isolate.rs:35-39`).
   - `viola send` stays outside the sandbox. viola's socket directory under the kept `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is a
     filesystem path, reachable across the network namespace.

6. **The readings, in order** (`CX`'s shape, `mod.rs:1546-1654`):
   1. The first frame: `box`, `modal`, `trust`. A trust form or no box → `refused: shape`, stopping before any
      send.
   2. `session-start` awaited.
   3. `net-ns`: `own` when the snapshot's `pid` and `child_pid` (viola's own `snapshot.json`) both read a
      `/proc/<pid>/ns/net` different from the rig's; `shared` when either equals it; `unread` otherwise. The
      wrapped `--contain`-less rehearsal reads `shared`.
   4. One send: the compiled `MT_PROMPT` literal written 0600 under the scratch, sent with `viola send sf-probe
      --json --file`. Its `prompt-submitted` is read back, giving `send-1` and `send-1-reply` (`R2`'s words).
   5. The first `turn-ended` past the send, awaited up to `SF_TURN_BOUND` (480 s, under the 900 s deadline;
      expected turn-end delay one to three minutes on 2.1.328, static, research §Containment):
      - `turn-end: stop-failure` when its data carries `cause`;
      - `stop` when it carries none (the API was reached);
      - `none` when no turn ended within the bound.
      `cause` is the word as written, or `none`. `turn-end-after-s` is the whole seconds from the send's reply to
      the line, a reading.
   6. `unknown-value-lines`: the count of `parse-rejected` lines whose `detail` is `unknown-value` in the
      instance's hook role file under the vhome's `diagnostics/`, read through `MAX_FRAME`, complete lines only;
      `unread` when the file cannot be read.
   7. The kept frame `send-1`, then the rig's stop (Ctrl-C into its own pty, the group kill past
      `STOP_KILL_AFTER`), then the standing teardown words (census, credentials, scratch, user-config).

7. **HELD — §C.4, the error-word capture (F1).** Only on the founder's word naming it:
   - The private config's settings.json gains one StopFailure hook running `viola-live-rig capture --out
     <scratch>/capture.ndjson`, beside `seed_capture`'s form (`isolate.rs:482-496`).
   - `capture.rs` writes, for a StopFailure payload: its key names (`[a-z_]{1,40}`, others counted), the error
     word when it is one of the CLI's 13 (a compiled list in the test-only crate) else `other`, and the byte
     lengths of `error_details` and `last_assistant_message`. Never a text.
   - The arm reads it into `captured-word` and `cause-matches: yes|no|unread`: the captured word mapped by
     `viola_agent_claude::hook::api_error_cause` against the `cause` read.
   - Without his word this step is not built: predicate 5 is read from the product path alone (Implementation
     notes, F1).

8. **HELD — §C.5, C3's cell-attribute reading (F2).** The founder answered «one `x` and one DEL before the send»
   (`inputs#I3` item 2). Before the send those keys move the wheel to the human, and the send is refused
   `human-typing` `(architecture · decision/byte-source-wheel-claim)`, so the payload reading would be lost. Only
   on his word on F2, at the place he names:
   - The box's prompt row cells past the glyph are read for their vt100 attributes alone: dim, italic, bold,
     inverse, foreground index. This gives one closed word `hint-attr` (`dim`, `italic`, `fg-<n>`, a `+`-joined
     set, `plain`, or `unread` with its reason).
   - One `x` is typed (grant `box`), its cell read into `typed-attr`, then one DEL.
   - `hint-told-apart: yes|no|unread`.
   - Never a cell's text. An unreadable reading is `unread` with its reason, a reading and not a red
     (`inputs#I3` item 2).
   - Without his word, `SF` types no key (`keys: none`) and C3 leaves with its named next reader.

title: D. The rehearsals (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`, keeps tests S1, S2, S3, S6)

data.head: ### D. The rehearsals (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`, keeps tests S1, S2, S3, S6)

body:
10. **`rig_rehearsal_sf_reads_a_stop_failure_turn_end_and_its_cause`** (CI, unwrapped):
    - The fake agent runs over a copy of `fixtures/claude/2.1.328` with a planted synthetic
      `StopFailure.default.json` whose `error` is `server_error` and whose texts embed the canary, under
      `--turn-stop --turn-fail default`.
    - Asserted: `send-1-reply` `ok`; `turn-end` `stop-failure`; `cause` `server-error`; `unknown-value-lines` `0`;
      `net-ns` `shared`; `keys` `none`; `census` `0`; credentials removed; scratch absent; user-config not
      `changed-by-rig`.
    - A second planted run, error word `no_such_word`, reads `cause` `api-error` and `unknown-value-lines` `1`. It
      is the case that can read the predicate red.

11. **`rig_rehearsal_sf_contained_reads_its_own_network_namespace`** (local; on CI it skips by a probe it prints):
    - It first runs the same no-op `bwrap` probe and prints `sandbox-probe: own` or `sandbox-probe: unavailable
      (<closed reason>)`. On `unavailable` it returns there; that is the only skip, and it is never silent.
    - Otherwise it runs `rehearse sf --contain` over the fake agent with `--turn-stop`, the recorded `Stop` turn.
    - Asserted: `net-ns` `own`, `box` `up`, `send-1-reply` `ok`, `turn-end` `stop` (the fake's Stop crossed the
      sandbox through viola's hook and socket), `census` `0`, scratch absent.

12. **`rig_rehearsal_sf_refuses_contain_without_the_sandbox_before_its_ledger_line`**: `rehearse sf --contain`
    with a `PATH` holding no `bwrap` (the child's `Command::env`) reads `refused: sandbox`, exit 3, and the case's
    ledger file absent.

13. The round follows the block order: the wrapped local rehearsal, the install read, the census, the build and its
    hashes, the sandbox probe, the host read, the scratch base read, then `SF`, then the census.
    - `SF-2` is fired only when `SF` was lost BEFORE its reading to a cause outside it (`refused: shape` on the
      first frame, the host stalling the start, the rig's token-window refusal). A token-window refusal is
      uncounted: implement stops and says so.
    - A red on predicate 1, 4, 5 or 6 is a reading, never a spare cause. It stops the round, and the spare stays
      unspent.
    - A `turn-end: stop` reading means the API was reached. The report says, in those words, that the start was
      NOT contained, and nothing is retried (`inputs#I3` item 6).
    - Each start is ledgered with `date -u` before it is made (the rig's own ledger line).
    - A CONTENDED host read with a neighbour named stops and is re-read, never retried into. This repository's own
      gate stall is no neighbour (verification-harness.md 2026-11-19).

14. After the round, implement writes `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-19-a-live-stopfailure-payload/evidence/stopfailure-reading.md`.
    It holds every predicate's word as read (1-7) and the turn-end delay. The C3 words and the captured word are
    included only where §C.5 and §C.4 were taken. The file states the outcome the wrap reads: green on 1-7, or the
    red reading named.
15. As the skeleton's operator entries (pre-push, hygiene, the clean-tree push, the CI read).
- none
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` — `keep_record` per version (§A); the sandbox argv and probe helper beside the scratch's own; under §C.4 the StopFailure capture's seed beside `seed_capture`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — `Arm::SF`, its labels and properties, the contained spawn in `run_child`, `arm_sf` and its readings, the unit cases (§C)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/capture.rs` — under §C.4 only: the StopFailure capture's closed words
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs` — under §C.5 only: the box row's cell-attribute word, never text
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — the `sf` arm word, the `SF` / `SF-2` labels, `--contain` on rehearse, the doc lines
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the three `sf` rehearsals (§D)
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — `--turn-fail <variant>` beside `--turn-stop` (§B)
Graph impact (research §Graph impact):
- `keep_record @ crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs:529` (`start`) and its unit test (`isolate.rs:1212-1230`);
- `of_label @ viola-live-rig.rs:226` and its four label tests;
- `run_child @ mod.rs:512`;
- no product crate reaches any changed symbol.
The block runs, in order:
- the formatter and the linter;

- the rig's library unit cases with `--no-fail-fast`, then the workspace unit layer (the `keep-version` control's
  entry);
- the rig rehearsals by binary;

- the live round: the wrapped local rehearsal, the install read, the census, the build, the sandbox probe, the host
  read, the scratch base read, `SF`, the census, `SF-2` (conditional, §E), then the operator-keyed census;
- the whole integration and E2E layers;
- the operator pass.
What is not run, and why:

- No smoke entry: no boot-path file changes. The fake agent's new option is argv-only and draws no new screen, so
  `cli_verify`'s recorded-screen cases are untouched; they run inside the whole integration layer all the same.

- No release check: `viola-e2e` and the fake agent are test-only, refused by `scripts/release-check.sh`, and the
  product graph is unchanged.
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 9).
Bounds and homes:

- The rehearsals wait through the file's existing helpers (`WITHIN` 18 s), under the integration profile's kill.
  The `sf` rehearsals pass `--deadline 15` as `Case::rig` does. The unit cases do not wait.

- The live `SF` passes `--deadline 900` under its entry's `timeout` 1200. The arm's `SF_TURN_BOUND` of 480 s holds
  the CLI's retries with room: one to three minutes expected, static, never measured.

- Every rehearsal runs under its case's own `/tmp` root. The live start runs under the rig's private scratch at
  `/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>/`, which names no `home` component.
**What the contained child can still write outside the scratch** (`inputs#I3` item 7):

- No witness reads the CLI's own writes under the home outside `~/.claude.json`. They are named here as the
  residual every private-config start already carries (the arch history's accepted CLI residual class), never
  claimed absent.

The live legs' non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of `SF`: the install read by path, the census, the
build with its hashes, the sandbox probe on a no-op child, the host read and the scratch base read. None primes
anything. The wrapped local rehearsal is the entry the live start rests on (`inputs#I3` item 5).

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, not entries (validation.md
check 4 (6)). Each reads «holds» only when its case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line; a `timeout` reading is not
«holds», and neither is an entry that is merely red.

| `keep-version` | `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` | `keep_record`'s per-version refusal (§A.1); implement quotes the exact text in the control record | `rig::isolate::tests::keep_record_refuses_a_standing_version_and_writes_nothing` | entry 4 (`bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit`, a workspace-building layer: testing.md 2026-11-13) | `--timeout 2400` |

| `sandbox-refusal` | `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` | the `refused: sandbox` return before the ledger line (§C.5) | `rig_rehearsal_sf_refuses_contain_without_the_sandbox_before_its_ledger_line` | entry 5 (the harness's integration layer, which builds the workspace) | `--timeout 2400` |

- Test homes on the Linux dev host (the founder's live answer, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer; a boundary widening): `target/e2e-home` is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so the fixture chain's sweep and drop and harness `cleanup` create and delete outside the working directory, each only a dir the test side itself made (by its owner record, its own temp dir or its session name prefix) or another build's stamp dir whose lock it takes with try_lock. The two keepers follow a linked base only when its target is absolute and one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refuse a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), each refusal a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts); they create it 0700 and remove nothing. `viola` never names the backing; no CI runner has the link. Accepted residual (a live round of `viola plugin install`): the round runs the CLI's own four commands (`claude plugin marketplace add` / `install` / `uninstall` / `marketplace remove`) at `--scope local`, a fresh count of four per rig, from a `proj/` that is its own git repo outside this work tree (on the e2e-home tmpfs, no ancestor `CLAUDE.md`): the CLI takes the local scope's project from the git work tree root, and a `proj/` inside the work tree meets the external-imports dialog after the trust dialog; the rig passes the folder-trust dialog by keys into its own pty only, never a desktop key, on the founder's own word anew for each chunk and by a closed argv grant (on a read screen at most 2 arrows toward the trust row and 1 Enter only when that row reads selected, one x and one DEL only in a ready box, any other key writing nothing; the founder's word binds the grant alone, and the rig's stop, Ctrl-C into its own pty or a no-key group kill, needs no word; on a wrapped start the keys move the wheel to the human, and `viola release <name>` precedes the driver's send); the CLI's writes are its own — its trust entry in `~/.claude.json` for each `proj/` whose dialog was accepted, the session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`, and after the removal its orphaned plugin cache `~/.claude/plugins/cache/viola/viola/<version>/` (re-written in place by a later install and uninstall), `installed_plugins.json` and `known_marketplaces.json` back as before (as measured on claude 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings); viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude` or into `~/.claude.json`, save `viola verify`'s own trust record for its fresh temp folder in the Claude config its child reads, only that record removed after (a SIGKILL leaves it); on a verified CLI only, `run` and `revive`'s start set `hasTrustDialogAccepted` alone (every other key kept) in the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder in the config its child reads, never for the user home folder or a folder the CLI's own walk reads as trusted, and that record stays. It is no product path and no standing permission: another such reading needs its own answer. The live rig runs its child under a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in its own scratch, seeded only with keys whose values come from the CLI bundle's own logic, none read from the user's config (used-config markers and, on every arm but VP, the browser-tools prompt turned off; VP leaves the browser-tools key out), with an environment built from a closed kept list of host names plus its own, and reads the user's `~/.claude.json` only after a moved stamp, searching it for rig-made needles, dropping the bytes and keeping one closed word; the VH arm runs under the real home and config, reads no credentials, keeps only key names and one needle word, prints no value, and needs an explicit home, Claude dir and user config. The live rig may read whether the key name `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` stands in its own private scratch config, printing written or absent, and never reads a value (a boundary widening, answered for the rig alone). The live rig's MCP recording arm keeps no CLI output (stdout drained and dropped, stderr kept only as a byte count and a SHA), and its MCP config is a private 0600 file inside the scratch, removed with it. The live rig's CX arm reads the session transcript through `MAX_FRAME`, counting only tags past the kept length and keeping no byte of it, and sends only through `viola send` under the rig's private config. A live session's screen frames are kept only under a gitignored local path, never in a work dir, a run dir or a commit; what lands is a closed-word summary per frame. The live rig copies the claude OAuth credentials file owner-only into its private scratch, reads only its expiry, refuses a start with under 20 minutes of token, removes the copy on every exit path, and writes no credential, host path or config value into any ledger, frame or summary; the VH arm, run under the real home, makes no copy and reads no credentials file. The live rig's SF arm runs the real claude inside a network-closed bwrap sandbox with its own network namespace; an absent or failing sandbox, or one sharing the rig's namespace, refuses the arm with `refused: sandbox`, exit 3, uncounted, before any credentials read or ledger line. The live rig's own hook capture (a ratified boundary widening) reads a payload under `MAX_FRAME` with the default JSON depth and writes one owner-only line: key names matching `[a-z_]{1,40}`, others counted; a UserPromptSubmit source word or a StopFailure error word of the CLI's 13, else `other`; two text lengths, never a text; a bad payload writes unread.

its argv-only `--transcript` creates `<exe dir>/transcripts/` at 0700 at start and gives the launch SessionStart a `transcript_path` to a seeded 0600 file named by its session id (replayed framing variants not rewritten), and every stamping `viola verify` against it (harness `boot` and the stamped-home helpers) passes it `--transcript` beside `--framing` (the framing-free verify helper passes none), and every test-started `viola verify`, `viola run` and `viola revive` and every harness boot stamping runs under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only, never the runner's real `HOME` (the harness's supervised wrappers of a stamped session too, under a session user home seeded with an empty config), the fake agent told that config file by `--trust-config` (a `--record` verify keeps the real `HOME` and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead); the exact verify echo probe command, like a stdout-tag local command under `--local-command-mode`, one stdout tag line appended to the last started session's transcript and no hook fired) for verify's six interactive runs (two capped test-only holds: `--stop-receipt-hold-ms`, 1 s, holds the Stop receipt for a race test; `--paste-hint-ms`, 10 s, holds a cleared screen after the long paste's turn; the test-only hold `--trust-record-blank` makes a start trusted by the trust record alone draw no screen, holding verify's Run F window open for a stop case;
